i.norm:
Verifies that {@link SequencesComparator} produces a minimal edit script.

The idea: start from a fixed sequence, then apply a known number of random mutations (each mutation is a single insertion or deletion) to derive a second sequence. Since the comparator implements Myers' shortest-edit-script algorithm, the number of modifications it reports must never exceed the number of mutations we actually applied.
Fixed seed so the random mutation sequence is reproducible across runs.
The "Shadok" alphabet: the only words that may appear in the sequences.
Indices into {@link #SHADOK_ALPHABET} describing the original, fixed sequence. (e.g. 0 -> "GA", 2 -> "ZO", ...)
Apply an increasing number of random mutations and check minimality each time.
Builds the fixed original sequence from {@link #ORIGINAL_WORD_INDICES}.

Returns a copy of {@code source} after applying {@code mutationCount} random single-element mutations. Each mutation is either an insertion of a random word at a random position, or a deletion of the element at a random position.
